📘 **Lesson 1**

This Java course introduces the basics of Java, including its history and key features like object-oriented programming with classes and inheritance, JVM bytecode for platform independence, strong typing, static compilation, garbage collection memory management, and extensive standard libraries available in Java API. The lesson aims to understand what Java is and set up your development environment by starting from setting up the JDK (Java Development Kit) on various platforms such as Windows or Mac OS X using an Integrated Development Environment like Eclipse IDE for writing, compiling, and running Java programs easily with built-in tools provided in these environments. It introduces a 'Hello World' program to demonstrate basic syntax of declaring variables, methods, classes along the way setting up foundational knowledge needed before moving into more complex topics such as data structures (arrays, lists) control flow statements like loops and conditions or exception handling mechanisms introduced later on by using `try-catch` blocks.

```java
public class HelloWorld {
    public static void main(String[] args) { // Entry point for a Java program where execution starts
        System.out.println("Hello World!"); // Print "Hello World!" to the console output, demonstrating basic syntax and I/O operations in java programming language
    } 
}
```

---
Say **'complete'** to mark this lesson done and continue.
Say **'exit course'** to leave the course.
Say **'progress'** to see your course progress.
